newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC says agrees $1 bln China chip venture. [corrected 12:04 gmt]
newsitem.headline: NEC says agrees $1 bln China chip venture. [corrected 12:04 gmt]

text.p: Japan's NEC Corp said on Wednesday that it had reached an agreement to set up a joint venture in China to produce semiconductors.
The project will cost a total of $1 billion, the company said.

NEC and its Chinese partner, Shanghai Hua Hong, will form the joint venture company in July to design, manufacture and market memory and logic semiconductors using NEC's 0.5- and 0.35-micron process technology, an NEC spokesman said.
NEC will contribute 28.6 percent of the venture's $700 million capital and Shanghai Hua Hong the remaining 71.4 percent, he said.
The venture and the plant will be located in Shanghai's Pudong district, he said.
(Corrects location of chip plant in accordance with correction by spokesman)
The new plant will be capable of producing 20,000 eight-inch wafers per month and start full-scale volume production in the first half of 1999, the NEC spokesman said.
The plant will produce dynamic random access memory chips and applied specific integrated circuits, among others, he added.
The agreement is a result of NEC's participation in China's five-year plan to develop its semiconductor industry, he said.
NEC was selected as the exclusive partner for plan, he said.
